transcript.content: Hi, welcome in. I'm Dr. Smith. Can you start by telling me what brings you in today?

Um... I guess they brought me in because of what's been happening at the warehouse. I keep doing things... like I'll just freeze with my arms up by the forklift. And I start copying the beeping sounds it makes, or doing the hand signals. 

Or I'll take the boxes and move them around in these strange little patterns. Even when everyone is yelling for me to stop, I just... I keep doing it. So, yeah. That's why I'm here.
Have you noticed anything unusual lately, like hearing voices that others don't hear, or having thoughts or beliefs that other people don't seem to share or understand?

No, I haven't noticed anything like that. I don't hear any voices or anything... just the normal warehouse sounds. And my thoughts seem fine to me. I don't think I believe anything that other people don't. 

It's really just the... the getting stuck and doing the hand signals and moving the boxes around, like I said. That's the only thing that's been unusual.
Have you had any recent medical illnesses, head injuries, or been using any new medications, drugs, or alcohol around the time these episodes started?

No, nothing like that. I haven't been sick or hit my head or anything. I don't really drink much, and I definitely haven't taken any drugs or started any new medications. I'm just... healthy, physically, I guess. Nothing new has changed there.
At what age did you first start noticing these repetitive movements or freezing episodes - did they begin in childhood, or did they start more recently as an adult?

It started more recently. I'm 20, so... yeah, definitely as an adult. None of this happened when I was a kid. 

I'd say the strange behavior at the warehouse, and... I guess the confusing talking people keep bringing up, it's all been happening for about six months now. So it's relatively new.
Do you have any ongoing medical conditions - like thyroid problems, seizures, autoimmune diseases, or other chronic illnesses - that a doctor has diagnosed or been monitoring you for?

No, I don't have any of those. No thyroid problems or seizures or... anything like that. I haven't been seeing a doctor for any chronic illnesses. Like I was saying before, physically I'm fine, so there's really nothing I'm being monitored for.
You mentioned people have been confused by your talking - can you tell me more about that? Do you notice your speech becoming jumbled, hard to follow, or going off in unrelated directions?

Yeah, I guess that happens. Like... at work. When my supervisor asks me which pallets are supposed to go on the truck, I try to explain it to him. But then my words just kind of... jump around. I'll start talking about the load sheet, and then suddenly I'm talking about my old house, and then fishing, and then... church boxes. And by the time I stop talking, he just looks at me, and nobody knows what I actually meant to say. It just comes out all mixed up.

Over these past six months, have you noticed yourself pulling away from friends or family, losing interest in things you used to enjoy, or feeling like your emotions have become flat or hard to express?

No, not really. I mean, I haven't noticed anything like that. I still hang out with my friends when I have time, and I haven't lost interest in my hobbies or anything. I don't feel like my emotions are flat, either. I feel pretty normal in that way, honestly. It's just the... the other stuff I mentioned that's been happening.

During these episodes, do you notice your alertness or awareness changing at all - like feeling drowsy, foggy, or confused at some times and clear-headed at others - or does your level of awareness stay pretty much the same throughout the day?

No, my awareness stays pretty much the same. I don't get drowsy or foggy or anything like that. I feel completely awake and clear-headed all day, even when the other things are happening. My mind doesn't really go in and out like that.

When you're doing these hand signals or freezing episodes, do you ever feel like something or someone else is controlling your movements, or do you have any particular explanation for why you're doing them?

No, I don't feel like someone else is controlling me. It's... it's definitely me doing it. I don't really have a good explanation for why, honestly. I just kind of... do the hand signals or stop moving. But nobody is forcing my body to do it or anything like that. I just don't really know why it happens.
Have you or anyone else noticed any other physical changes, like muscle stiffness, tremors, unusual movements, or loss of bladder control, around the time these episodes happen?

No, I haven't noticed anything like that. I don't get stiff or shaky, and there's definitely no issue with... you know, bladder control. It's really just the freezing up and the hand things. No other weird physical stuff going on.
